title: Found Unconscious

rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Patient unconscious — assess general appearance, cherry-red skin, signs of smoke inhalation.
rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych: Unconscious patient requires full neurologic exam to establish baseline.
rationale.Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs: Smoke exposure — evaluate for inhalation injury.
rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: CO poisoning can cause cardiac ischemia.
rationale.Arterial blood gases: ABG with COHb is the definitive diagnostic test.
rationale.Lactate, serum: Elevated lactate suggests tissue hypoxia; if markedly elevated, consider concurrent cyanide poisoning.
rationale.100% O2 non-rebreather: Start immediately — reduces COHb half-life to ~1 hour.
rationale.Hyperbaric O2 (if severe): Consider for COHb >25%, LOC, neuro deficits, cardiac ischemia, pregnancy.
rationale.Monitor for neurologic sequelae: Delayed neurologic syndrome can occur 2-40 days post-recovery.

hpi: Ama Serwaa is a 7-year-old girl with no known past medical history who was found unconscious in a burning building by firefighters. She was exposed to dense smoke and had loss of consciousness at the scene. On arrival to the emergency department she remains unresponsive with cherry-red skin.
hpi_narrative: Ama Serwaa is a 7-year-old girl with no known past medical history who was found unconscious in a burning building by firefighters. She was exposed to dense smoke and had loss of consciousness at the scene. On arrival to the emergency department she remains unresponsive with cherry-red skin — a hallmark of carbon monoxide poisoning. The clinical question: with a history of enclosed-space fire exposure and altered mental status, what is the severity of her CO poisoning (COHb level), are there concurrent inhalation injuries or cyanide toxicity, and does she meet criteria for hyperbaric oxygen therapy?
practice_hpi: Ama Serwaa is a 7-year-old girl with no known past medical history who was found unconscious in a burning building by firefighters. She was exposed to dense smoke and had loss of consciousness at the scene. On arrival to the emergency department she remains unresponsive with cherry-red skin.
physical_exam: 7-year-old girl unresponsive, cherry-red skin discoloration, soot on face and clothing, pediatric body proportions on ED stretcher
CO poisoning can cause cardiac ischemia even in children — monitor for arrhythmia
Smoke inhalation risk — pediatric airway is narrower and more reactive; evaluate for wheezing, stridor, carbonaceous sputum
Unconscious — pediatric neuro exam shows altered mental status; baseline deficits must be documented
Cherry-red discoloration; check for burns and soot

patient_voice.history: 7-year-old girl found unconscious at scene — unable to provide history. Firefighters report heavy smoke, enclosed-space fire. Parents en route to hospital.
